2️⃣ How It Works — typically proxies: same address, changeable underlying logic.

Xi Jinping Draws a Red Line: Dialogue With Trump Is Key to Avoiding US-China War


Xi Jinping used his meeting with Trump at the White House to call for closer communication between Washington and Beijing, warning that growing rivalry between the two powers must not spiral into a military confrontation.

Speaking at the start of the summit, Xi argued that the United States and China should maintain open and sustained dialogue despite their differences. He said greater mutual understanding, trust and cooperation could help the two countries avoid what is known as the “Thucydides Trap” — the risk of conflict when a rising power challenges an established one.

Xi said both nations would benefit from cooperation and suffer from confrontation. He specifically called for regular communication between the US and Chinese militaries, along with stronger mechanisms for managing and preventing crises.

The Chinese leader also pointed to areas where the two countries could build closer ties. Among his proposals was an invitation for 100,000 young Americans to travel to China over the next five years for educational and exchange programs.

The appeal comes as Washington and Beijing remain locked in intense competition over artificial intelligence, trade and technology, while tensions surrounding Taiwan continue to complicate the broader relationship. 

Both governments have imposed tariffs and other restrictions on trade, while the US has tightened controls on advanced semiconductor technology and equipment exported to China.

Trump, meanwhile, welcomed Xi and Chinese first lady Peng Liyuan to the White House, describing his relationship with the Chinese president as a strong personal friendship. 

The US president said the two sides had made progress on several issues, including efforts to create what he described as a more balanced trading relationship and expand market access for American farmers and ranchers.

Trump also said security, technology and artificial intelligence would be among the subjects discussed during the visit. He has recently used the term “super intelligence” to describe the next stage of AI development.

Xi also emphasized his personal rapport with Trump, saying the two leaders had maintained contact and developed mutual respect. He said both sides should work toward a stable and constructive relationship and steer US-China ties in a predictable direction.

The White House summit followed a highly ceremonial welcome for Xi, who arrived in Washington with Peng Liyuan. Trump had personally traveled to Andrews Air Force Base the previous evening to greet the Chinese leader upon his arrival.
Despite the diplomatic pageantry, the meeting comes against the backdrop of significant strategic competition. 

Washington continues to restrict China's access to advanced chips, semiconductors, software and chip-making equipment, while trade tensions remain unresolved.

A temporary US-China tariff truce that was due to expire in November has also been extended until February, according to US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. 

The extension keeps negotiations between the world's two largest economies open as both sides seek further concessions.

The talks in Washington therefore combine diplomatic outreach with continuing economic and technological rivalry, with Xi presenting dialogue and crisis-management mechanisms as key tools for preventing competition from turning into direct conflict.

🔔 South Korea targets November review for second stage crypto legislation 

🌐 South Korea’s Financial Services Commission has set November for a National Assembly subcommittee review of the Digital Asset Framework Act, rejecting claims that work on the country’s second stage crypto legislation has been delayed. According to Seo Na yoon, head of the FSC’s virtual asset division, the regulator and lawmakers are moving in the same direction on legislation covering digital asset issuance and distribution, including stablecoins. Speaking at a National Assembly seminar in Seoul on Sept. 22, Seo said differences remain over when the government will submit its draft, but the November review remains part of the planned timetable. 

⚡️ “The FSC is not dragging its feet at all. We share the same view,” Seo said, responding to criticism over the pace of the legislation. “The direction has already been set, and while detailed discussions may be necessary in the process, there is certainly no intention on the FSC’s part to delay.”

🔗 Seo said the regulator wants the legislation passed quickly and expects discussions to proceed using bills that lawmakers have already introduced alongside the government’s proposal. Ten digital asset and stablecoin bills are currently pending in the National Assembly, giving lawmakers existing proposals to work from before the government completes its version.
